answer: The cheapest defence against cloned agents is making cloning expensive. Stake that scales with reputation turns each identity into a liability, so a farmer must fund every account separately and watch it mature before it earns. Think of it as a relic the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single spiral of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a velvet of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
